questions.questionText: You ____ wear a helmet while riding a two-wheeler.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses a legal or strong obligation.

questions.questionText: ____ I come in, madam?
questions.explanation: 'May' is used to ask for polite permission.

questions.questionText: She ____ swim when she was five years old.
questions.explanation: 'Could' is the past of 'can' for an ability in the past.

questions.questionText: If it rains tomorrow, we ____ the picnic.
questions.explanation: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb.

questions.questionText: If I were you, I ____ accept the offer.
questions.explanation: Second conditional: if + past, would + base verb.

questions.questionText: If he had studied, he ____ the exam.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.
questions.shortcut: If + had pp, would have pp.

questions.questionText: If water is heated to 100 degrees, it ____.
questions.explanation: Zero conditional for general truths: if + present, present.

questions.questionText: You ____ not smoke in a hospital.
questions.explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition.

questions.questionText: It is not necessary to carry cash, so you ____ not carry it.
questions.explanation: 'Need not' expresses absence of necessity, matching the stem.

questions.questionText: He ____ be at home; his car is outside.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses a strong logical deduction.

questions.questionText: It ____ rain this evening; the sky is cloudy.
questions.explanation: 'May' expresses a possibility.

questions.questionText: You ____ to respect your teachers.
questions.explanation: 'Ought' is always followed by 'to' and expresses moral duty.

questions.questionText: I wish I ____ a bigger house.
questions.explanation: After 'wish' for an unreal present, the past tense is used.

questions.questionText: I wish I ____ the exam last year.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' for an unreal past takes the past perfect.

questions.questionText: If I ____ rich, I would help the poor.
questions.explanation: In unreal conditions the subjunctive 'were' is used for all subjects.

questions.questionText: Unless you ____ hard, you will not succeed.
questions.explanation: After 'unless' the present simple is used for a future condition.

questions.questionText: He suggested that she ____ a doctor.
questions.explanation: After 'suggest that', the base form (subjunctive) is used.

questions.questionText: ____ you please pass the salt?
questions.explanation: 'Could' is a polite request.

questions.questionText: You ____ have told me earlier; now it is too late.
questions.explanation: 'Should have + pp' expresses criticism of something not done.
questions.shortcut: should have = regret/advice in the past.

questions.questionText: She ____ have left already; the lights are off.
questions.explanation: 'Must have + pp' expresses a strong deduction about the past.

questions.questionText: He ____ be sixty; he looks very young.
questions.explanation: 'Cannot' expresses a strong impossibility.

questions.questionText: I ____ get up early when I was in school.
questions.explanation: 'Used to' denotes a past habit that no longer exists.

questions.questionText: I am used to ____ up early.
questions.explanation: 'Be used to' (accustomed) is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: If you ____ me, I would have helped you.
questions.explanation: The result clause 'would have helped' needs the past perfect in the if-clause.

questions.questionText: I would rather ____ at home than go out.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' is followed by the bare infinitive.

questions.questionText: He ____ not come yesterday because he was ill.
questions.explanation: 'Could not' is the past of 'cannot' for inability.

questions.questionText: ____ I help you with the luggage?
questions.explanation: 'Shall I' is used for offers with the first person.

questions.questionText: The students ____ submit the form by Friday.
questions.explanation: An official obligation uses 'must'.

questions.questionText: If she ____ earlier, she would have caught the train.
questions.explanation: The result 'would have caught' requires the past perfect.

questions.questionText: It is time we ____ for the airport.
questions.explanation: 'It is time + subject' takes the past form of the verb.

questions.questionText: He asked whether he ____ use my phone.
questions.explanation: In reported speech 'can' changes to 'could'.

questions.questionText: If you heat ice, it ____.
questions.explanation: A general truth takes the present simple in both clauses.

questions.questionText: You ____ better see a doctor about that cough.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' gives strong advice and takes the base verb.

questions.questionText: Were I the Prime Minister, I ____ reduce taxes.
questions.explanation: Inverted second conditional 'Were I' is followed by 'would'.
